hypothesis: Table 2 Augmented counts represent additional images, not final class totals.
supporting_evidence: Table 2 separates Train images and Augmented Images; p.72857 defines augmentation as creating new data from existing data; Section IV-C says its training/validation counts consist of original and augmentation images.
contradicting_evidence: No Table 2 column definition, formula, or note states whether the displayed augmented values are additions, per-class targets, or another measure.
missing_evidence: A paper-defined counting rule and stage-by-stage class ledger linking original, train, and generated images.

hypothesis: Table 2 Augmented counts include original training images.
contradicting_evidence: The table uses separate Train images and Augmented Images headings; Section IV-C describes counts as consisting of original and augmentation images, implying distinct components there, but not defining the table column.
missing_evidence: Explicit definition of whether each table cell is inclusive or incremental.

hypothesis: Section IV-C counts refer to a later processing stage than Table 2 counts.
supporting_evidence: Section IV-C describes augmentation on training data followed by a further training/validation division; it reports totals after describing this sequence.
contradicting_evidence: Table 2 has no stage label; the paper never says its values are pre-augmentation, post-augmentation, or earlier than Section IV-C.
missing_evidence: Explicit Table 2 measurement stage and a direct mapping to Section IV-C totals.

hypothesis: A training/validation split or filtering operation explains the difference.
supporting_evidence: Section IV-C explicitly describes a later train/validation division; image preprocessing including hair removal is also described elsewhere.
contradicting_evidence: A split alone preserves the combined count. No dataset-record filtering, count removal, or exclusion of 1,965 records is documented in the inspected text.
missing_evidence: A documented count-changing operation, its timing, and affected records/classes.

hypothesis: The paper contains an arithmetic or reporting inconsistency in the Table 2 / Section IV-C totals.
supporting_evidence: Conditional on NV=0 and treating Table 2 Train+Augmented as the same pool, arithmetic differs by 1,965. Table 2 also satisfies Original=Testing+Train in all classes.
contradicting_evidence: The paper does not establish that the compared figures measure the same cohort or stage; separate section totals are arithmetically self-consistent. The augmentation-method count also varies between 13 and 20, but does not explain image counts.
missing_evidence: Definitions of table columns, cohort identity, and processing stages; author clarification of the 13/20 method-count scope.

hypothesis: The NV = 00 entry changes the reconciliation.
supporting_evidence: The exact printed literal is ambiguous; no paper note defines it, so a literal augmented sum cannot be calculated.
contradicting_evidence: If conditionally interpreted as zero, the Train+Augmented vs. Section IV-C train+validation difference remains 1,965; there is no evidence for another numeric interpretation.
missing_evidence: Author/source clarification of the literal and its intended arithmetic role.

hypothesis: Available evidence is insufficient to distinguish the explanations.
supporting_evidence: The paper gives no Table 2 augmented-count definition or class-level bridge to Section IV-C; no explicit count-changing filtering step was found; the NV literal is undefined.
contradicting_evidence: The narrative offers a plausible order of operations, but does not establish that Table 2 and Section IV-C are the same cohort/stage.
missing_evidence: A versioned cohort manifest, column definitions, augmentation ledger, partition membership, and explanation of NV 00.
